avatars.program:
Keep planche quality high and repeatable, and build the dip goal from both ends: one heavy reserve day and one specific +60 kg volume day. Lower body stays productive but low-cost for BJJ, and Zone 2 is kept easy enough to recover from.

Weeks 2-4: add a little hold time, a little density, or a small load bump only if positions stay clean. Week 4 consolidates with slightly harder top work, not a full deload.

Pain/substitutions: keep all planche work on parallettes. If wrists feel irritated, shorten the hold slightly before changing the shape, and use an extra warm-up set. If front squat feels unusually beat-up from BJJ, swap that day to Goblet Squat at similar effort. Avoid adding any extra hard conditioning.

avatars.program:
Keep every rep crisp and stop skill sets before shape breaks. Weighted Chin-up stays the anchor; Human Flag gets direct practice twice weekly; lower body work is enough to maintain MMA useful strength/power without extra fatigue.

Weeks 2-4: make the small jumps shown if bar speed and positions stay solid. If a day feels suppressed from MMA, keep the same load and hit the lower end of the rep target rather than forcing progression.

Elbow guidance: use a fully warmed supinated or slightly angled grip that feels best, avoid extra pulling volume beyond what is written, and stop any Weighted Chin-up set if medial elbow pain rises above mild discomfort. If flag side-pressure irritates the elbow or shoulder, swap that day to Assisted One-Arm Pull-up is not appropriate here; instead reduce hold time on One-Leg Tuck Human Flag by 1-2 seconds and keep shape strict. If Front Squat wrists feel beaten up, use straps on the bar.
